problem_meta.instruction: Assess the following protein sequence and provide a brief report on its primary characteristics:
problem_meta.ground_truth: A summary of the protein's main attributes with the input amino acid sequence reveals: Extracellular circulating Tat can be endocytosed by surrounding uninfected cells via the binding to several surface receptors. Endosomal low pH allows Tat to cross the endosome membrane to enter the cytosol and eventually further translocate into the nucleus, thereby inducing severe cell dysfunctions ranging from cell activation to cell death. problem_meta.agent_answer:
1. [✓] Analyze sequence properties and retrieve functional annotations/homologs.
2. [✓] Synthesize a concise functional summary, distinguishing evidence from inference.

### Brief report

The 119-amino-acid sequence is an **exact sequence match** to reviewed **Tat protein P27982** from simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV; AGM3 isolate). Its predicted molecular mass is about **13.4 kDa**. It is **basic** (theoretical pI 9.4; estimated charge at pH 7 of +9.7) and hydrophilic by sequence-based estimates.

Tat is a **viral transcriptional activator**: the curated annotation describes recognition of the TAR RNA element on nascent viral transcripts and recruitment of the **P-TEFb (cyclin T1–CDK9) complex**, promoting RNA polymerase II elongation and production of full-length viral RNA. A Pfam scan identified the **Tat domain (PF00539)** at residues 22–60. The reference annotation places it in the host-cell **nucleus and nucleolus**.

These functional details are supported by the exact match to the annotated reference protein; the physical-property values are sequence-derived estimates and may not reflect modifications or cellular context.
